theorem_title: Removing observations preserves a target-blind pair
natural_language_statement:
Let $I,X,V$ be arbitrary types with distinguished zeros in $X,V$, subtraction operations, observation maps $r_i:X\to V$ and target $q:X\to V$. Assume the maps preserve zero and subtraction, and subtraction in $V$ is zero exactly when its arguments are equal. For a selected set $S\subseteq I$, let $K_S=\{d\in X:\forall i\in S,\ r_i(d)=0\}$. Let $A,B\subseteq I$ satisfy $A\subseteq B$. Write $\operatorname{Blind}(S)$ for the existence of two states whose target values differ but whose observations agree at every index in $S$. Then

$$
\operatorname{Blind}(B)\Longrightarrow\operatorname{Blind}(A).
$$

This monotonicity lemma permits restriction of the observer coalition while retaining a witness of target nonidentifiability.
